name: Rezi
description: AI-assisted resume builder aimed at ATS-friendly job applications. Free / Pro ~$29/mo / Lifetime ~$149; Rezi Enterprise for orgs (300+ organizations claimed). Forbes-ranked #1 AI resume builder (company-stated). Founded May 2015, US, VC-backed. ~4.5M estimated users on TrustMRR.

mentions.evidence: ~$251,264 MRR, 10,418 active subscriptions, ~$222,910–$224,316 L30, ~$10,260,842 all-time, ~60% L30 profit margin. Last sync Oct 3, 2026 ~04:15 Warsaw (02:15 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Own one career-bureaucracy artifact (resume, cover letter, visa packet, LinkedIn audit) with freemium + lifetime + enterprise upsell. Volume seats print even at low ARPU.

whyItPrints: Job-hunt utility with brutal volume — 10k+ paying subs and $10M+ all-time. "Make my PDF pass the ATS" is evergreen career bureaucracy glue, not a novelty chat app.
whyThisMatters:
Job seekers build a resume meant to get through an applicant tracking system. You upload one you have, or start from a blank page. Sections and spacing stay plain as you type, which is what those systems can parse.

A score splits the resume by section. Paste a job ad and it lists the missing keywords. There's also a checker, a bullet writer, a summary, a cover letter, a resignation letter, job search, and interview practice. A Chrome extension fills applications. You can pull the resume into other AI tools.

Try it free, no card. After that it's a monthly plan, a one-time lifetime purchase, or an enterprise plan for companies. They say Forbes picked the builder first, and they put the audience at 4.5 million people. The company started in the US in May 2015 and has taken outside funding.
